_meta.source: research/sema; main page ('Sema: when the hash is the word')

failure_modes: Near-duplicate words fragment the vocabulary when agents mint without searching
A dominant agent's words crowd out others, turning self-organisation into central control
gloss: A shared vocabulary shaped only by the interactions of the agents that use it
invariants: Only agent interactions add to or reshape the vocabulary
A word's identity is fixed by its content, so shared use implies a shared definition
mechanism: Agents mint words for consistent patterns of behaviour, ideas or traits, and reuse the words others minted. No authority defines the vocabulary: it is an instance of {{self_organisation}}, shaped only by agent interactions, as human language is. Every interaction can change it, and its interdependencies are too large for any agent to solve. Because each word is content-addressed, agents can verify they share a definition, and the paths agents trace through the words expose their reasoning.
